sources.title: Sutskever, Martens, Dahl, Hinton (2013). On the importance of initialization and momentum in deep learning. PMLR 28(3):1139-1147.
sources.scope: Section 2, equations (1)-(4): displacement HB and Nesterov gradient evaluated at theta+beta*d. No deep-network experimental claim is attributed to the four-row teaching example.

sources.title: Bubeck (2015). Convex Optimization: Algorithms and Complexity. Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning 8(3-4):231-358.
sources.scope: Section 3.7, theorem 3.18 and estimate-sequence argument; standard strongly-convex constant coefficients and function-gap bound. Original x/y sequences mapped to teaching z/theta, indexing shifted to t=0. Convex-only O(1/t^2) requires its appropriate changing-coefficient algorithm.

sources.title: Lessard, Recht, Packard (2016). Analysis and Design of Optimization Algorithms via Integral Quadratic Constraints. SIAM Journal on Optimization 26(1):57-95, author corrected version 2017.
sources.scope: Section 2 state realization, proposition 1 and Appendix A eigenmode reduction and quadratic tuning, section 4.6 and Appendix B strongly-convex nonquadratic heavy-ball counterexample. Course two-step stability/Jury proof and all four-row examples independently derived. Standard strong-convex NAG setting distinguished from quadratic-optimal NAG tuning.

sources.title: PyTorch 2.7 official documentation: torch.optim.SGD; installed PyTorch 2.7.1+cpu source.
sources.scope: First momentum buffer copies gradient without dampening; subsequent buffer beta*v+(1-tau)*g; lr outside buffer; Nesterov uses g+beta*v and requires positive momentum with zero dampening; foreach/fused explicitly disabled. Installed _single_tensor_sgd source inspected and actual float64 CPU comparisons executed.

limits: No source illustration or long source passage copied. Data, derivations, exact hand tables and figures are original.
Official 2.7 documentation link points at the 2.7 series; the actual patch-version behavior was checked in installed 2.7.1 source and execution.
Only finite synthetic full-gradient experiments; no claimed real-task, GPU, stochastic or universally nonconvex acceleration.
Copyright of source documents is separate from the authored tutorial.
